items.question: Check 1: among parity runs that reach 90 % test accuracy, the fraction in which the planted set {x_S, yhat} activates (>= 95 %).
items.definition_used: Denominator: parity-k2/k3/k4 objects with finite t_test_acc90 (90 % test accuracy reached within the budget). Numerator: the object has an 'activation' row in ri_events whose subset_json equals the planted set {x_i : i in S*} U {yhat} (S* re-derived from the task's data_seed, = curve ground_truth; matches_gt True). Left-censored activations count (the registered text says only 'activates'); the alternative excluding them is also given. Events cross-checked against detect_events(curve, alpha=0.01).
items.literal_result: 288 of 288 runs (parity-k2 100/100; parity-k3 120/120; parity-k4 68/68); 0 parity runs did not reach 90 % test accuracy.

overall 288/288
parity-k2 100/100
parity-k3 120/120
parity-k4 68/68
excluding left-censored activations: 288/288
runs not reaching 90 % test acc: 0
items.interpretation: The instrument detects the planted (k+1)-order interaction in every run that learned.
items.caveats: All 288 parity runs reached 90 % test accuracy, so the denominator is every run; the check cannot probe runs that fail to learn. Amendment 1 does not change check 1.

items.question: Check 2: RI onset and Fourier onset of the planted subset fall on the same or adjacent checkpoint (|index gap| <= 1) in >= 90 % of parity runs.
items.definition_used: RI onset index t_RI = position in curve.steps of the planted subset's first activation event (events.py: event step = steps[t0], t0 the first of the two consecutive active checkpoints, active = q <= 0.01 and bias-corrected RI >= min_effect; equals step_hi). Literal Fourier onset = first checkpoint index with |f| >= eps0 = 0.044714 (single-mode RI = min_effect = 0.001; root found numerically). Amended (A): first t with gate(t) and gate(t+1), gate = [R - 1/(2N) >= min_effect] and [min(1, m chi2_1.sf(2 N R)) <= alpha], R = ln2 - h_b((1+|f|)/2), m = meta n_candidates, N = meta min_effect_n = 4096, alpha = 0.01. Gap = t_RI - t_F (checkpoint indices); agreement iff |gap| <= 1. Denominator: all 288 parity runs; a missing onset would be censored at index T (step budget) (none occurred). Alternatives reported: Fourier onset requiring the sign of the final coefficient; RI onset per Amendment C (first non-left-censored activation with the final sign).
items.literal_result: 216 of 288 runs agree within one checkpoint (parity-k2 28/100; parity-k3 120/120; parity-k4 68/68); gap histogram {'0': 155, '1': 61, '2': 42, '3': 18, '4': 11, '5': 1}.
items.amended_result: 284 of 288 runs agree within one checkpoint (parity-k2 96/100; parity-k3 120/120; parity-k4 68/68); gap histogram {'-3': 1, '-2': 3, '-1': 26, '0': 255, '1': 3}.

items.interpretation: Literal: the bare-threshold Fourier onset precedes the RI onset by more than one checkpoint in 72 runs, 72 of them in parity-k2 (literal gaps are never negative), as Amendment 1 A predicted: RI also needs the BH q-value and persistence, and for k = 2 the coefficient grows gradually through the bare threshold. Amended (decides): with the same gate the two onsets agree in 284 of 288 runs; gap histograms literal {'0': 155, '1': 61, '2': 42, '3': 18, '4': 11, '5': 1}, amended {'-3': 1, '-2': 3, '-1': 26, '0': 255, '1': 3}. The amended disagreements are all k = 2 at n = 16 or 32 (gap -2 or -3: RI earlier). fce53621af616dbf (n 16, lr 0.03, seed 6: RI idx 20 step 38, Fourier idx 22 step 49, of which -2 from BH q < m*p and 0 from RI plug-in vs R(f)); ff9af0024cc1ac32 (n 16, lr 0.1, seed 0: RI idx 10 step 11, Fourier idx 13 step 16, of which -1 from BH q < m*p and -2 from RI plug-in vs R(f)); 7a186b27ec789432 (n 16, lr 0.1, seed 7: RI idx 12 step 14, Fourier idx 14 step 18, of which -2 from BH q < m*p and 0 from RI plug-in vs R(f)); c3eae965d4d2c00f (n 32, lr 0.1, seed 5: RI idx 22 step 49, Fourier idx 24 step 63, of which -2 from BH q < m*p and 0 from RI plug-in vs R(f)).
items.caveats: With uniform probes RI and the Walsh coefficient are near-deterministic functions of each other, so this is a consistency check of the pipeline (thresholds, q-values, checkpoint indexing), not a comparison of methods. The amended gate's q stand-in m*p is conservative (>= the BH q), so residual gaps are expected to be RI earlier than Fourier (negative). Checkpoints are log-spaced; one index is a step ratio of up to ~1.3. The single-mode relation RI = ln2 - h_b((1+|f|)/2) is only approximate while the network still has lower-order Walsh components on subsets of S (largest |RI plug-in - R(f)| = 0.0178 nats, mid-transition in a k = 3 run); this, not a pipeline bug, moves a few onsets by one or two checkpoints.

items.interpretation: No planted activation is left-censored: at step 0 the planted coefficient is at most 0.0142 in absolute value, bias-corrected RI is 0 nats in every run and q at least 0.989, far from the detection threshold, so the RI onsets of checks 1-2 are not affected by initial offsets (Amendment 1 C's issue is about Markov pairs).
items.caveats: Counts come from ri_events (ri_before NaN) and agree with detect_events' left_censored flag in all 288 runs.

items.question: Does any parity run fail to learn?
items.definition_used: Failure to learn = t_test_acc90 NaN (90 % test accuracy never reached) or final_test_acc < 0.9; also checked: light-curve final test accuracy, final planted |f| and RI at the last checkpoint.
items.literal_result: 0 of 288 runs fail to learn; min final test acc 1.0000; min final |f| 0.9988; min final planted RI 0.6869 nats (ln 2 = 0.6931).
items.interpretation: Every parity run learned its parity within the budget (latest 90 % test-accuracy crossing per region: {'parity-k2': 768.0, 'parity-k3': 29905.0, 'parity-k4': 8535.0} against budgets {'parity-k2': 20000, 'parity-k3': 60000, 'parity-k4': 150000}).
items.caveats: Learning is judged from the light-curve summary and the RI curve; final test accuracy is 1.0 for all runs, so there is no failed-learning subgroup to check the instrument on.
